Four — move fingers, toes, shoulders, and eyes. Five — eyes open, present, ordinary, clear. The session has ended. ... edits.old:
Use this checklist when a person, advertisement, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic pull, or inner voice is pressing too hard.

“I notice influence is happening. I do not need to obey it or attack it. I can slow down. I can ask what is being presupposed. I can ask who benefits. I can notice what my body is signaling without assuming what it proves. I can ask what love, truth, humility, and ordinary life would require.

If this is true, it will survive questions. If this is love, it will survive boundaries. If this is guidance, it will survive sleep. If this is for me, it will not require me to abandon my adult self.”

Before acting, ask:

Is there urgency?

Is there secrecy?

Is there shame?

Is there a threat of exclusion?

Is there a promise of specialness?

Is there sexual charge?

Is there spiritual superiority?

Is there a demand for money, sex, loyalty, silence, or obedience?

Is there a narrowing of choices?

Is questioning treated as betrayal?

Is resistance pathologized?

Is ordinary life being downgraded?

Is the child part being seduced, scared, or rescued?

Is the adult self still allowed to say no?

Several yes answers mean slow down. Don’t deepen trance or make an irreversible decision. Return to the room, body, food, sleep, time, and counsel.

A good guide increases your adult self. A bad guide replaces it. A good guide can tolerate your no. A bad guide calls your no resistance, ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, or proof that you need more of their guidance.
edits.new:
Use this checklist when something is pressing on you too hard, whether it’s a person, an ad, an ideology, a spiritual teaching, a romantic pull or a voice inside you, stuff like that. You could say something like, “Okay, I notice that I’m being influenced. I don’t have to obey it, and I don’t have to attack it either. Let me slow down and ask what it’s taking for granted, and who it benefits. My body is telling me something, but I don’t have to decide yet what that proves. And what would love, truth, humility and ordinary life need from me here?

If it’s true, it can handle my questions. Would real love mind my boundaries? And real guidance will still be there after I sleep on it. Anything that’s really for me won’t ask me to give up my adult self.”

Before acting on it, look for the usual signs, like urgency, secrecy, shame, a threat that you’ll be left out or a promise that you’re special, that kind of thing. Is there a sexual charge, or spiritual superiority? Be wary if it demands money or sex from you. Demands for your loyalty or your silence are signs too, and so is any demand for obedience.

It’s a warning if your choices are being narrowed. Same if asking questions gets treated as betrayal, or your resistance gets treated like a pathology. Or if ordinary life starts to look small next to it, like the dishes and your friends don’t matter anymore.

Notice whether your child part is being seduced or scared. Being rescued counts too. And is your adult self still allowed to say no?

If you see several of these, slow down. Don’t go deeper into trance, and don’t make a decision you can’t undo. Just come back to the room and your body for a while. Then eat, sleep, give it time, get some counsel and so on.

You can tell a good guide because your adult self gets stronger with them. And can they take your no? A bad guide can’t. They take your adult self’s place, and they’ll call your no resistance, ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, you name it, or proof that you need more of their guidance.

edits.old: bring in a “nurturer”, “protector”, “leader”, etc to help you either change the “tone” of the interaction, set boundaries, or help you figure out how to live your life in a better fashion, feel free to do so. You don’t have to talk to them, just use them to get whatever function you need that you aren’t able to do on your own.
edits.new: bring in a “Nurturer”, “Protector”, “Leader”, etc to help you either change the “tone” of the interaction, set boundaries, or help you figure out how to live your life in a better fashion, feel free to do so. You don’t have to talk to them, just use them to get whatever function you need, and if you can’t do one yet, borrow it.
edits.published: The Nurturer can change the tone; the Protector can carry out a boundary; the Leader can point toward the life you want. They don’t each need a speech. When a capacity isn’t available, borrow that one function. Use the Witness only if you need it to begin; don’t restart a step you can already do.
edits.diagnosis: the inner-adult sweep (fix-20261021/CONFLATION-SWEEP.md, finding 2; Joel, 17:56: "check the guide for that conflation"): the sentence before says "If you can identify any “protector” parts, talk to them", in the same lowercase, quoted form, so "bring in a “protector”" reads as one more of those guards. The published text and the rest of the guide give the three roles capitals. And the stance check's conflict in the same paragraph (r1/STANCE.md, conflict 1): "use them to get whatever function you need that you aren't able to do on your own" makes the three roles outside helpers, where the guide has them as your own adult functions ("I don't mean them as if there were really three people in you") and a missing one borrowed (the published "When a capacity isn't available, borrow that one function"); now "and if you can't do one yet, borrow it"

edits.old: It could also be an inner voice of a parent that you are picking up, and it is trying to enforce a rule about how you should be to belong to them. Again, it isn't useful to argue with this part, but find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable 'grown up' voice.
edits.new: It could also be the voice of your inherited inner parent that you are picking up, and it is trying to enforce a rule about how you should be to belong to them. Again, it isn't useful to argue with this part, but find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable 'grown up' voice of your own.
edits.published: The voice may be the inherited parent enforcing an old belonging rule. Don’t argue with it. Ask which rule it is enforcing and what ordinary evidence would make the new adult voice more believable.
edits.diagnosis: the inner-adult sweep (fix-20261021/CONFLATION-SWEEP.md, finding 3; Joel, 17:56: "check the guide for that conflation"), the pattern Joel fixed in "When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice": the parent's voice was just named, so "a more believable 'grown up' voice" can read as a more convincing version of that same voice (a parent is a grown-up whose voice you picked up). The published text says "the new adult voice". Two changes, as in his fix: his name for the internalized voice, "inherited inner parent", and "of your own" for the adult one
